purpose: Gradual, instrumentation-verified curriculum proving each Deegen (arXiv:2411.11469) mechanism engages, staged from bare interpreter dispatch through full-system closure and adversarial fallback-safety. Separate from quench-bench/micros/ (the neutral perf-regression corpus, which this does not modify or replace).
instrumentation_source: execution_trace.rs snapshot(), emitted to stderr as 'QUENCH_EXEC_TRACE {json}' at process exit when QUENCH_EXEC_TRACE=1 is set. See deegen-verify.mjs.
instrumentation_gaps: Stage 5 (tier-up) and stage 6 (OSR-entry) currently have no per-run, CLI-observable counter for *live* tier promotion or OSR firing: machine.rs's TierState/tier_profile() and is_osr_entry are in-process APIs, not surfaced through execution_trace's snapshot() JSON emitted at process exit. These stage cases are correctness-only until that gap is closed (would need a small additive counter in execution_trace.rs, e.g. tier_transitions / osr_fires, feature-gated like everything else in that file). Stage 4's kernel-hit counters (lanes.l1.kernels) are the closest existing proxy for build-time fast-path/counted-loop admission, not a literal RegionKey-level counter — see docs/deegen-alignment.md.

stages.name: interpreter-dispatch
stages.description: Baseline interpreter dispatch correctness: arithmetic, branch, loop control, calls, exceptions.

stages.name: call-inline-cache
stages.description: Call-site inline caching: monomorphic hit, bounded polymorphic, megamorphic degrade, re-stabilization, recursion.

stages.name: property-generic-ic
stages.description: Property-access generic IC (λi/λe split): monomorphic, polymorphic, megamorphic, guard invalidation, get/set interleave.

stages.name: fast-path-kernel-admission
stages.description: Type-check elimination / fast-path kernel admission and its hostile-input fallback.

stages.name: tier-up-threshold
stages.description: Interpreter-to-baseline-JIT tier-up threshold boundary behavior (correctness-only; see instrumentation_gaps).

stages.name: osr-entry
stages.description: OSR-entry motivating shape: single-invocation hot loops, and structured loops that must not attempt OSR (correctness-only; see instrumentation_gaps).

stages.name: full-system-closure
stages.paper_section: whole-program, project analog to paper §8's 44-benchmark evaluation
stages.description: General neutral programs exercising several mechanisms simultaneously at realistic scale.

stages.name: fallback-safety-adversarial
stages.description: Inputs designed to defeat every fast path, proving guarded/unknown fallback stays correct.

cases.title: Straight-line arithmetic recurrence
cases.mechanism: Plain arithmetic dispatch: every opcode should execute via the fast/compact lane.

cases.title: Branch ladder dispatch
cases.mechanism: if/else and switch-style branching: dispatch stays on the fast lane across all branch outcomes.

cases.title: Loop control: break and continue
cases.mechanism: Nested loops with break/continue: control-flow opcodes stay on the fast dispatch path.

cases.title: Repeated plain function call
cases.mechanism: A hot call site to one stable function: exercises call dispatch and site-level quickening at baseline.

cases.title: Exception throw/catch/finally
cases.mechanism: A hot loop that throws and catches on a subset of iterations: exercises the unwind/exception path deliberately.

cases.title: Monomorphic call site
cases.mechanism: One callee called repeatedly at the same call site: should install and hold a monomorphic call IC.

cases.title: Bounded polymorphic call site
cases.mechanism: A call site rotating across 3 stable callees: should become bounded polymorphic, not degrade.

cases.title: Megamorphic call site (distinct closure per call)
cases.mechanism: Every call sees a freshly-created closure: call IC should degrade past its bound and stay correct.

cases.title: Stable call site that switches once
cases.mechanism: A call site monomorphic for the first half, then permanently switches callee: expect one re-install, not thrashing.

cases.title: Recursive self-call
cases.mechanism: Recursive calls to one function object: the recursive call site should be monomorphic by construction.

cases.title: Monomorphic property get
cases.mechanism: Repeated get of the same property on objects sharing one stable shape.

cases.title: Monomorphic property set
cases.mechanism: Repeated set of the same property on objects sharing one stable shape.

cases.title: Polymorphic property get (3 shapes)
cases.mechanism: Property reads rotate across 3 distinct, stable shapes: expect bounded polymorphic behavior, not degrade.

cases.title: Megamorphic property get (many shapes)
cases.mechanism: Each object has a uniquely-shaped property set: property IC should degrade to megamorphic and stay correct.

cases.title: Guard invalidation mid-loop
cases.mechanism: A stable shape is mutated by adding a new property mid-loop: the IC's guard must re-probe, not trust a stale state.

cases.title: Interleaved property get and set
cases.mechanism: Get and set on the same stable-shape property in one loop body: proves the idempotent probe is reused correctly for both.

cases.title: Numeric add-heavy hot loop
cases.mechanism: A tight numeric-add loop shaped to admit a fused fast-path kernel over the arithmetic sequence.

cases.title: Numeric add hostile (mixed types)
cases.mechanism: Same loop shape as case 17, but operands alternate number/string: must defeat fast-path admission and still compute the correct (string-concatenated) result via the complete fallback.

cases.title: Mixed arithmetic operators loop
cases.mechanism: Subtract/multiply/divide in one hot loop: exercises fast-path admission for operators beyond add.

cases.title: Stable property-chain hot loop
cases.mechanism: A guarded property-access chain on one stable shape, hot enough to be a fast-path kernel candidate.

cases.title: Hostile polymorphic property chain
cases.mechanism: Same access chain as case 20, but shapes rotate every iteration: must defeat guarded-region admission and stay correct via fallback.

cases.title: Function invoked just under the promotion threshold
cases.mechanism: Invoke a small function 20 times (below the current 32-retired-bytecode TierState threshold): should stay in the interpreter tier.

cases.title: Function invoked well over the promotion threshold
cases.mechanism: Invoke a small function thousands of times: should cross the tier-up threshold and promote to the baseline tier.

cases.title: Many distinct cold functions, one call each
cases.mechanism: 50 distinct functions each called exactly once: none should individually cross the tier-up threshold.

cases.title: Single-invocation hot loop (paper's OSR motivating case)
cases.mechanism: A function called exactly once, containing a very hot loop: tier-up-on-entry can never fire (only one invocation), so only OSR-entry mid-loop could promote this.

cases.title: Structured for-in loop, single invocation
cases.mechanism: A structured (for-in-shaped) hot loop called once: per the documented ForI exclusion, this must not attempt OSR-entry and must still be correct via the ordinary loop gateway.

cases.title: Nested hot loops, single invocation
cases.mechanism: A function called once with a hot outer loop and a hot inner loop: exercises OSR-entry admission at more than one back-edge in the same invocation.

cases.title: Linked-list and tree traversal
cases.mechanism: Object-oriented traversal over a small tree and a linked list, bounded shape set, hot enough to tier up.

cases.title: Recursive numeric algorithm mixed with calls
cases.mechanism: A recursive Ackermann-lite function mixing arithmetic and call dispatch under load.

cases.title: Small event-queue state-machine simulation
cases.mechanism: A generic task-queue simulation (structurally similar to classic VM benchmarks, but sized and shaped as a neutral general program, not a fixture-detecting kernel).

cases.title: Mixed array/object/Map workload
cases.mechanism: Interplay of arrays, plain objects, and Map: exercises several data-API fast paths in one program.

cases.title: String-heavy parsing-like loop
cases.mechanism: Tokenizing and accumulating over strings: tests string/control interplay together.

cases.title: Polymorphic dispatch inside a hot loop
cases.mechanism: A hot loop dispatching to one of several handler shapes each iteration: combines call-IC polymorphism with a hot loop.

cases.title: Proxy-wrapped object defeats shape assumptions
cases.mechanism: A Proxy intercepting property access must defeat any shape-based fast path and still produce correct trapped results.

cases.title: Getter with an observable side effect
cases.mechanism: A property getter with a side effect must run exactly once per access, even under repeated access at a hot call site.

cases.title: Accessor swapped mid-loop via defineProperty
cases.mechanism: A plain data property is redefined as an accessor mid-loop: subsequent reads must observe the new accessor, not a stale cached slot.

cases.title: Call target reassigned mid-loop with side-effecting arguments
cases.mechanism: A previously-monomorphic call site's target is reassigned partway through, with an argument expression that has a side effect: both the dispatch target and the side effect must stay correct after reassignment.

cases.title: for-in over inherited, own, and deleted properties
cases.mechanism: Prototype-chain iteration with deletions mid-loop: must enumerate exactly the correct live key set at each step, defeating any static-shape enumeration shortcut.
